title: Price pressure produces widespread household adaptation while personal and national economic judgments diverge
source_unit: Federal Reserve Survey of Household Economics and Decisionmaking adult respondent, 2025

observations.period: 2025 SHED; household price response and material hardship

denominator.unit: weighted adult population estimate; publication percentages use the adult respondent frame

observations.method: Federal Reserve 2025 SHED published population estimates; multiple price-response actions could be selected and are not mutually exclusive.
observations.uncertainty: Self-reported cross-sectional survey measures do not identify the specific price, bill, income shock, displaced need, or later recovery; estimates may vary by subgroup and question universe.
observations.subgroup: All adult respondents; lower-income, Hispanic, disabled, and middle-aged adults reported greater price-related worsening in the source discussion.
observations.counterinterpretation: A reported adaptation can be voluntary or protective rather than deprivation, and multiple actions cannot be assigned to one causal price event.

observations.period: 2025 SHED; personal financial well-being versus national economic judgment

denominator.unit: weighted adult population estimate; publication percentages use separate question universes

observations.method: Federal Reserve 2025 SHED executive-summary comparison of personal financial well-being and national economic assessment.
observations.uncertainty: The questions measure different constructs and are not a panel causal comparison; party identity, information, local conditions, and question framing may shape national judgments.
observations.subgroup: All adult respondents, with reported declines among some low-income, young, and Black adults in personal well-being.
observations.counterinterpretation: A negative national assessment alongside okay personal finances can reflect reference groups, political interpretation, media, or expectations rather than direct household price exposure alone.

related_sources.claim: The broader 2025 SHED report supplies additional financial-condition, work, and economic-view context.
related_sources.access_boundary: The source families measure distinct question universes; no single price event or political action is identified.

boundary: This record establishes 2025 survey-reported price adaptation, bill/food hardship, personal financial status, and national economic judgment. It does not establish a causal price-to-politics path, trust change, benefit adequacy, recovery, or a same-household longitudinal effect.
